en.headline: Hong Kong opens International Academy of Policing to train local and overseas officers
en.dek: Chief Executive John Lee said the academy will train about 1,000 officers each year, including 200 from overseas, through programmes and leadership forums.
body: Hong Kong opened its International Academy of Policing on Wednesday, with Chief Executive John Lee officiating at the ceremony at the Hong Kong Police College.

Lee said the academy would deepen international police exchanges through training programmes, police leadership forums and other initiatives. The target is to train some 1,000 officers each year, including about 200 overseas law enforcement personnel.

The academy plans more than 20 major international training programmes and forums by the end of next year, including a senior leadership forum called ConvergeHK expected next April. Police Commissioner Chow Yat-ming said the academy would help connect global law enforcement agencies through professional training.

The facility is located within the existing Police College in Wong Chuk Hang and will coordinate existing and new international courses covering areas such as leadership, tactics, counter-terrorism and investigations.

zh.headline: 香港國際警務學院正式成立 每年培訓約千名警務人員
zh.dek: 行政長官李家超主持開幕典禮，學院目標每年培訓約1000名警務人員，當中包括約200名海外執法人員。
body: 香港國際警務學院周三正式成立，行政長官李家超在香港警察學院主持開幕典禮。
李家超表示，學院將透過培訓課程、警務領導論壇及其他外展活動深化國際警務交流。目標是每年培訓約1000名警務人員，當中包括約200名海外執法人員。
學院計劃在明年年底前舉辦超過20個重點國際培訓課程及論壇，包括預計明年4月舉行的高層領導論壇ConvergeHK。警務處處長周一鳴表示，學院將透過專業培訓把全球執法機構緊密聯繫起來。
學院設於黃竹坑警察學院內，將統籌現有及新的國際課程，涵蓋領導、戰術、反恐及刑事調查等領域。
